999.t: Bass drum duets with Baptiste Mosley
999.s: Jones and Baptiste Mosley took spontaneous drum solos on parades and he explains how.
999.ch: Black Benny, brass bands and bass drum
999.q: I just started up one spur of the moment, just like you said. Started up one time, we was playing a one o'clock jump in the brass band. So, guys was taking solos, different ones. So, Bapt said, give us a solo. And we just taking one, him and I, and from then on we just continued doing it. Different…

956.t: Playing in a dance band: following the drums and bass
956.s: Henry says he follows the drum and bass and likens playing to a conversation of instruments.
956.q: You go by the drum beat. Whatever. If you say one, two, three, four, one, two, three, four, you play that when it hit, you're on that bouncing style.

876.t: Down strokes and Dixieland bass and drum rhythm
876.s: The down stroke is rhythm; the Dixieland bass and bass drum play first and third until the hot last chorus.
876.q: No, no, no. Because many of the double strokes. Now and then you'll hit a double stroke. For instance we'll say on, the way we used to use, used to add lead, even on the rhythm instrument, was on the last course what we call the hot chorus. All the instruments play as they should. The rhythm, play…

312.t: The rhythm section must know the tunes
312.s: Why rhythm players and drummers must know the changes.
312.q: Oh yeah that’s very true. The rhythm section, even the drummer. I judge the quality of a drummer by the way that he plays the tune, the accents that he puts in at the right place at the right time. And some drummers are good drummers but they just don’t have a feel for the music or they don’t know…

535.t: Playing bass and bass-drums interaction; dragging and Joe Hunt with Dexter
535.s: Having played bass helps him hear how bass and drums relate; he stays flexible with different rhythm sections and tells the Joe Hunt and Dexter Gordon story about dragging.
535.q: Yes. Well that and how to hook up with the drums, you know, how to play time and where to put the beat. That is even more crucial, of course because I played piano I’m hearing the chords and with my left hand I can play bass notes. But hearing the dialogue or the interaction between the bass and…

805.t: Booker on time, pulse and tension in bass playing
805.s: Booker describes playing within a pulse, with rhythm, melody and harmony interdependent, creating flow and tension while fitting the band.
805.q: Yeah. Well there is a meter, a pulse, that when you’re playing you’re playing within, you know? And at the same time you’re playing harmony or you’re playing notes that go with —

981.t: The bass player's role and keeping time in a rhythm section
981.s: Fleming says the bass is the base of the harmony and that time is a consensus of the rhythm section, not one player's job. He gives his students no list of rhythm sections to study.
981.q: Well you say main, well let me try. What it turns out to be, the predominant utterance of the rhythm section. In other words, it’s not either or. I mean some people play like that but to me that’s an inferior approach. I don’t think that way. I got the time, you got the time, although there have…

1002.t: Sun Ra's free approach: rhythm, groove and synthesizers
1002.s: Harrison describes collective sound, odd meters and bass lines, and Sun Ra's celeste and early synthesizers.
1002.q: From what I remember it was just notes. And you’d harmonize from your imagination. It could have been anything. You harmonize — you might hear it as a major, somebody might hear it as a minor, you know. But it was about a collective, a collective sound. And what we worried about was the — he was…

835.t: Favorite session bassists and finding common ground
835.s: Humphrey names Abraham Laboriel and Jimmy Johnson and says drummer and bass player must adjust to find where to put the beat.
835.q: Well yeah, it gets tricky there, but I know that when you talk about pop music for example they talk a lot about the time is here but the back beat is sort of on the back side of where the beat is, and that gives the effect of — the time is steady but it’s got this sort of other pocket, it’s like…

442.s: Keep a quiet groove behind Shakur; with Eddie Gomez and Evans he played straight ahead like behind a horn.
442.q: Well the main thing is you just kind of keep the groove going. I know when I played with Hassan with Ellington, he always liked it when I played, just keep a nice background feel happening. You’re not going to get too busy or too loud, because you don’t want to cover him up you know. But you know,…

585.t: How a bassist reads a gig: groove, Dick Hyman, Jeff Hamilton
585.s: She describes finding what each gig requires, keeping the groove steady, and following drummers like Jeff Hamilton; Dick Hyman gives guidelines without instructions.
585.q: Um. Well it’s funny, there are different ways to lead a band, you know, and now that I’m a band leader myself a lot I’m learning how to do it and get the results and get the respect and everything, and there are some people, like when I was up here last time I worked with Dick Hyman here, and I…

557.t: Drummer and bass player on the beat
557.s: The drummer and bass should be like one person, right on the beat, giving soloists a foundation.
557.q: Oh I think everybody should think ahead. If you read, you have to read ahead. You can’t be playing here and reading here, you’ve got to see that and then you’re looking over here you know what I’m saying? But as far as playing, the drummer and the bass player should be just like this, just like one…

549.s: Using Lawrence Lucie and Jo Jones, he assigns roles to bass, guitar, drums and piano.
549.q: Oh yeah. Jon Hendricks went crazy over that this morning here at the IAJE so I now realize that he wants me to put it down on paper, and to mail it to him. But you’re getting a thing. But this is really, you know I was raised by Jo Jones the drummer in the Basie band, and someone we haven’t…

813.t: Rhythm section chemistry with Michael Moore, Dave Frishberg and Bob Haggart
813.s: How he fits with the bassists and pianist at this weekend's party, including recreating a recording that had no drums.
813.q: Well I haven’t played with Michael Moore yet. I will do that tonight. And I’ve only played with him once and that was at this jazz party when it was still in Pennsylvania, about 1985. That won’t be any problem. He’s a real light bass player.

575.t: What a bass line does for the horn player and the band
575.s: Smith explains how a bass line outlines the chords by playing the root or third, and how other rhythm players depend on it. Rowe agrees the bass player decides where the band goes.
575.ch: Bass function and the film role
575.q: Well it’s kind of all a choice. I mean you just play the line, you just follow the line. I mean the way I play I’m just following the line and, but I’m at the age now where I can go, “Hey!” And also they don’t play at that tempo anymore. Nobody does.

943.t: Feeling time with different bass players
943.s: He explains adapting to bassists who play behind or on top of the beat, and Miles's quintet shifting tempo.
943.q: Yeah. I’ve learned a lot. I know when things are right because — I can’t tell you why. It’s a physical sensation and I know when it’s wrong too. So what I did is first of all I realized that my time is not God’s answer to time. And that if I had to be anything, or the only way that I could say that…

108.s: A steady rhythm section matters; amplified basses and busy drummers hurt.
108.q: It can. It can drive the band, make the band really perform well, or it can drive the band up the wall if it’s the kind of rhythm section where people in the rhythm section tend to go their own separate ways. You get a lot of that these days, because you have amplified bass violins now, the Fender…

8.t: The most important thing in jazz bass: four beats
8.s: Garland says rhythm and four beats from bass and drums behind the front line, with guitar and piano, are what the Dixieland rhythm section features.
8.ch: New Orleans style and bass playing
8.q: Well I tell you, we take the rhythm section, we work together, especially the drum and that bass. We must have them four beats. You take a man taking a hot chorus, you understand, they want them -- wants that rhythm, you know --
